## The question

[LaTeX is trying to write to python file although just call file to be read](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/737626/latex-is-trying-to-write-to-python-file-although-just-call-file-to-be-read), asked by [Joe](https://tex.stackexchange.com/users/36270/joe) on TeX Stack Exchange (2025-02-21; [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)):

> For some reason, in the code below, LaTeX is overwriting my `.py` file although I am just trying to call the `.py` file.  Here is the contents of the `pycode_batch_noreg.py` file:
>
> ```python
> import network3
> from network3 import Network
> from network3 import ConvPoolLayer, FullyConnectedLayer, SoftmaxLayer
> training_data, validation_data, test_data = network3.load_data_shared()
> mini_batch_size = 10
> net = Network([
>         FullyConnectedLayer(n_in=784, n_out=100),
>         SoftmaxLayer(n_in=100, n_out=10)], mini_batch_size)
> net.SGD(training_data, 60, mini_batch_size, 0.1, 
>             validation_data, test_data)
> ```
>
> And here is the contents of the LaTeX file:
>
> ```latex
> \documentclass{article}
>
> \usepackage{calc}
> \usepackage{listings}
> \usepackage{pdfpages,graphicx}
> \usepackage{mdframed}

> \definecolor{light-gray}{gray}{0.92}
> \definecolor{mygray}{RGB}{243,243,244}
>
> \renewcommand\lstlistingname{Python Code}

> \lstdefinestyle{pycode}{

>     breakatwhitespace=false,
>     breaklines=true,
>     captionpos=b,
>     basicstyle=\color{Black}\ttfamily,
>     commentstyle=\color{LimeGreen},
>     stringstyle=\color{WildStrawberry},
>     frame=leftline,
>     framesep=0mm,
>     xleftmargin=3mm,
>     framesep=2mm,
>     framerule=0mm,
>     abovecaptionskip=5mm,
>     aboveskip=\baselineskip,
>     belowskip=\baselineskip,
>     basicstyle=\ttfamily\scriptsize,
>     classoffset=1,
>     morekeywords={var, func, extends, import, as,from},
>     keywordstyle=\color{BurntOrange}\bfseries,
>     classoffset=2,
>     morekeywords={network3},
>     keywordstyle=\color{blue}\bfseries,
> }
>
> \newcounter{pylst}
> \newtcblisting[use counter=pylst]{pycode}[3][]{%
>         enhanced,noparskip,breakable,colback=light-gray,colframe=gray,opacitybacktitle=.8,%
>         fonttitle=\bfseries,before upper={\hspace*{-1em}\includegraphics[height=\baselineskip]{example-image-a}~#2},%
>         title after break={\centering\footnotesize\itshape\strut Python Code~\thetcbcounter--~continued},%
>         listing only,listing options={style=pycode, xleftmargin=-1mm},%
>         after upper={\par\centering Python Code~\thesection.\thetcbcounter},
>         arc=0pt,outer arc=0pt,boxrule=0pt,leftrule=1mm,
>         listing file = {#3}, #1}
>
> \newenvironment{brokenlst}{\addvspace\baselineskip}{\addvspace\baselineskip}
>
> \begin{document}
>
> \begin{pycode}{Baseline Python Code.py}{./python/pycode_batch_noreg.py}
> \end{pycode}
>
> \end{document}
> ```
>
> Can you tell me how not to overwrite my py file?  Thanks!
:::

Expanding my comment to an answer, it seems like the setting the `listing file` key for a `\tcblisting`-listing command *writes to* rather than *reads from* the indicated file. 

To list and pretty-print the contents of a file, you want a command like `\tcbinputlisting`. So change `\newtcblisting` to `\newtcbinputlisting`.

The other thing is that commands like `\newtcbinputlisting` create *commands*, not environments. So the first mandatory argument to `\newtcbinputlisting` needs to be a command name like `\pycode` and not a plain string like `pycode`.

Once you've made those changes, you can change the invocation to:

```latex
 \pycode{Baseline Python Code.py}{pycode_batch_noreg.py}
```
